title: Introduce atomic retry policy registry and shimless cross-SDK interoperability
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Adds a centralized, atomic retry policy registry and cross-language shims to improve parity between Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Backwards-compatible defaults preserved; opt-in for advanced policy composition. Includes documentation and test coverage across SDKs.
description:
Motivation: different SDK teams have drifted in retry configuration semantics and telemetry emission. This causes operational surprises when services switch SDKs or when a single app uses multiple SDKs.

What this PR does (high level): introduce an atomic RetryPolicyRegistry in the platform core and provide lightweight, shimless adapters in Python/TS/Go SDKs that read and apply policies consistently. Telemetry hooks are standardized so a single retry decision across languages emits the same metric tags. The registry supports composition (e.g., default + tenant overrides) and deterministic precedence; policies are immutable once installed to avoid races.

Checklist: - [x] Core retry registry implementation (platform/runtime) - [x] Python adapter and tests - [x] TypeScript adapter and tests - [x] Go adapter and tests - [x] End-to-end CI matrix (py/ts/go) - [x] Docs and changelog entry - [x] Telemetry tag parity verified

Compatibility notes: default behavior is unchanged for existing consumers. New behavior (policy composition and atomic installs) is behind an opt-in flag in each SDK (enable_atomic_retry_registry = true). The registry API is intentionally small: register_policy(id, spec), get_policy(id), install_atomic_batch(list_of_policies).

Dev notes: see inline code snippets below for the minimal adapter surface used by each SDK. The adapters are intentionally thin—no language-side reimplementation of decision logic—so most of the logic lives in the registry (platform).

References: Linear ENG-2145 (retry harmonization), internal doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2145/retry-harmonization, previous PRs touching retry RFCs: #214007, #110010.

review_comments: Diego Morales (review): This is a big win for parity. Two asks: 1) ensure the immutability contract is enforced across concurrent installs (we should avoid a window where half-installed batches are visible). 2) add a defensive TTL on registry cache entries in SDKs so a long-closed connection doesn't hold stale policy forever.

Anika Shah (author): Implemented atomic batch installs with a version token returned by install_atomic_batch; SDKs must fetch policy by version to avoid seeing partially-installed batches. Added optional TTL param in SDK adapters; default is 24h. See commits b3e4c7a and f4b8a66.
Liam Chen (review): Code + tests look good. Minor: in the TypeScript client please avoid Promise<any> in the public surface — prefer well-typed PolicySpec.
author_replies: Anika Shah: Addressed typing in TS (policySpec typed in registryClient.ts). Expanded unit tests to cover typed round-trip. See commit d9f2c11.
Anika Shah: Added integration test for concurrent installs (tests/interop/test_retry_policy_matrix.py) and CI matrix entry to run it across py/ts/go.
Anika Shah: Left migration guidance in docs/sdk/retry.md showing how to opt-in and roll back safely.
requested_changes: Diego Morales: Add an explicit observability test to assert identical telemetry tags emitted from the three SDKs for the same decision path.
